🏋️‍♀️ The Skinnify Story
Our founder Christian grew up in Frankfurt, Germany. Looking around, he noticed something striking: so many of the women in his life — his mom, his sister, his friends — wanted to get fitter, lose weight, and build muscle, but kept running into the same wall. They didn't have the time, the motivation, or the consistency to make the gym work.
The idea hit him during his own workout. He was using resistance bands and thought: what if these were built into everyday clothing? What if women could get the benefits of resistance training passively — while walking the kids to school, cooking dinner, or sitting at their desk? Fitness without the extra time or effort.
The idea was personal too. Christian was a difficult kid growing up and put his mom through a lot. She barely had time for herself, let alone the gym. He built Skinnify for women like her: busy, hardworking, often overlooked — so they could do something good for their bodies just by getting dressed.
🛍️ Our Products
What started with a single product — leggings with built-in resistance bands — has grown into a full collection of resistance-integrated clothing: leggings, sleeves, shoes, and more. We're on a mission to revolutionize how women do fitness by turning daily life into a workout.
🌟 Skinnify's Core Values
💡 Innovation – We design new, groundbreaking clothing with built-in resistance to revolutionize fitness.
🔥 Effectiveness – Our products help people burn more calories & get fitter with every step.
🌍 Accessibility – We make fitness accessible to everyone — even the busiest and least motivated.
🎉 Fun – We make exercise feel effortless and enjoyable.
✅ Quality – Our products are built to last — high-quality, durable, and reliable.

Operate with an AI-first approach across your whole workflow, using automation to accelerate content generation, personalization, segmentation, decisioning, and analysis
Run experimentation and data-driven optimization as a default across every program, measuring true incremental impact and continuously sharing learnings and insights across the team. Own your metrics and reporting end-to-end
Work closely with Product, Customer Education, PMM, and GTM so that lifecycle campaigns and content land as native, timely, and genuinely useful to users

Obsession with craft and a high-quality bar for content. Able to create copy and visual storytelling across lifecycle channels that resonates and drives action
Growth mindset with a drive to launch fast and iterate, building systems that evolve over time. Comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment and ambiguity

At Affirm, we exist for the moments that matter—giving people a clear, predictable way to pay over time, with no hidden fees, no surprises, and no tradeoffs on what matters most.
About the Brand & Communications team
Brand and Communications shapes how the world sees Affirm, and how Affirm chooses to be seen. That means showing up where perception takes shape: in culture and press, across Affirm's owned and paid channels, and within the company. We hold a high standard for craft and clarity, and we work to make Affirm a brand people understand, trust, and are proud to choose.

We're looking for a Brand Manager to turn business priorities and consumer insight into campaigns that shift perception and drive measurable demand. You’ll own campaign strategy from brief through launch and retros, aligning partners, sharpening priorities, and ensuring every expression builds a more distinctive, trusted and effective Affirm brand.

Own campaign strategy and architecture for priority brand and partner moments, including co-marketing projects with key merchants and ongoing merchant and promotional campaigns outside the major seasonal moments. Translate business goals, audience insight, and brand strategy into briefs and recommendations that shape how Affirm invests in these moments, not just how individual campaigns execute.
Drive early strategic thinking and lead brief development for partner campaigns, shaping how Partner Marketing, Product Marketing, Creative, Social, Paid, and Comms work together on audience, narrative, channel roles, and definition of success. Advise these teams on tradeoffs and complex calls, and review creative to ensure execution teams have what they need to build and ship excellent work.
Set campaign GTM strategy and investment priorities across brand and partner moments, determining how Brand Operations resources timelines and workflow and how channel leads allocate budget.
Build a learning culture. Define what's working across campaigns and turn it into reusable frameworks and standards that make every future effort stronger.
Own brand measurement and reporting in partnership with paid and analyst functions, both for brand overall and campaign by campaign. Maintain the integrity of the brand health tracker, hold execution partners accountable to the brief, and give leadership a clear, recurring read on what's working and what needs to change.
What We Look For
You have 8-10 years in brand marketing, integrated marketing, or a closely related discipline, with experience managing full campaigns from strategy to launch, ideally at both an agency and in-house teams.
As a natural creative thinker and problem solver yourself, you know how to partner and get strong creative out of a team. You've briefed and run creative work that landed sharp, on strategy, on budget and on time.
You have a track record of building brand awareness, equity, and differentiation through data and consumer insight, and can evaluate performance against business KPIs.
You're comfortable operating in a complex, matrixed marketing organization, and you’re capable of building alignment across cross-functional partners through influence.
You use data to develop and articulate a clear point of view, while staying collaborative and open to new information changing your mind.
Bonus. Experience with extending campaigns to global markets, and working in fintech, financial services, or another trust-sensitive category is a plus.

s.h: As a Head of Product Marketing, you will
s.t:
Define Amplitude’s product narrative and positioning: Own the overarching product marketing strategy and point of view across our multi-product portfolio, including analytics, Statsig, and proactive agents. Develop a differentiated point of view and way to bring the company’s worldview to life, staying close to how teams at all stages of maturity curve are building.
Lead GTM strategy for major products and launches: Partner with Product and Engineering to bring new products and capabilities to market—from positioning and messaging to launch strategy, enablement, customer proof, and adoption. Set a creative approach that caters to the audience, market, and maturity of each product.
Build and coach a high-performing AI native PMM function: Set the team’s priorities, operating cadence, and bar for quality while developing PMMs into stronger strategists and storytellers.
Turn customer and market insight into strategy: Develop a deep understanding of our customers, competitors, and market dynamics. Bring those insights back to Product, Engineering, and GTM to influence the product and experiments.

s.h: You'll be a great addition to the team if you have
s.t:
You’re a player-coach by nature—you can set strategy and lead a team, but you’re equally comfortable writing the positioning, building the narrative, jumping into a customer conversation, or helping shape a demo.

You are high agency . You don’t wait for the perfect brief or a fully formed playbook; you push your team to make the first draft, test it with customers, learn quickly, and keep improving.
You thrive in ambiguity and change . You’re comfortable operating at the intersection of Product, Engineering, Sales, and Marketing, and you know how to create clarity when the product and market are still evolving.

Senior Marketing Manager, Global Marketing – Oncology (LUMAKRAS)

Let's do this. Let's change the world.
In this vital role, the Senior Marketing Manager, Global Marketing will be a key member of the Global Oncology Marketing team supporting LUMAKRAS during an important period of brand evolution and launch preparation.
This role offers a unique opportunity to help shape global strategy for two anticipated first line launches in NSCLC and metastatic colorectal cancer, each presenting distinct strategic and commercial challenges. The successful candidate will help determine how LUMAKRAS can compete in an increasingly dynamic NSCLC market while also addressing treatment practice and behavior barriers that may affect adoption in CRC.
Reporting to the Global Marketing Director, this individual will have meaningful strategic responsibility across both first line indications, leading global marketing workstreams that translate market, customer, competitive, and clinical insights into clear strategic choices and launch plans. The role will provide broad exposure to global brand strategy, launch planning, lifecycle management, competitive strategy, and cross functional leadership.
The Senior Marketing Manager will also play an important role in connecting strategy to execution across the organization. This includes managing key Integrated Brand Team and Brand Working Group forums, partnering with regional and affiliate teams to incorporate market perspectives into global strategy and launch preparation, and ensuring decisions and plans are translated into coordinated action.
As clinical evidence, competitive dynamics, and customer insights evolve, this individual will help continuously refine the brand strategy and associated global deliverables to ensure LUMAKRAS remains responsive to a changing treatment landscape.

The responsibilities below represent key focus areas of the role and are not intended to be exhaustive. As business needs evolve, the successful candidate will demonstrate flexibility and agility by taking on additional responsibilities and leading new initiatives that support the needs of the organization.
Global Brand Strategy and Strategic Planning
Lead global marketing workstreams supporting development, refinement, and execution of the LUMAKRAS global brand strategy across NSCLC and CRC.
Translate customer, market, competitive, clinical, and affiliate insights into clear strategic implications, choices, and recommendations for the brand.
Partner with the Global Marketing Director and cross functional stakeholders to identify emerging opportunities, challenges, and strategic considerations across the LUMAKRAS lifecycle.
Continuously assess assumptions underlying the brand strategy and recommend adjustments as the treatment landscape, evidence base, customer behaviors, and competitive environment evolve.
Help define where and how LUMAKRAS can create differentiated value across indications and markets, connecting strategic choices to measurable business objectives.
First Line Launch Strategy and Readiness
Support global launch strategy and readiness workstreams across anticipated first line NSCLC and CRC indications.
Help shape strategies that address the distinct adoption challenges of each market, including increasing competitive intensity in NSCLC and treatment practice and behavior barriers that may affect adoption in CRC.
Translate launch strategy into clear critical success factors, key decisions, risks, mitigation plans, and global deliverables.
Partner across Marketing, Medical, Value & Access, Commercial Excellence, Regions, and Affiliates to integrate functional and market perspectives into global launch planning.
Support global to local launch readiness by ensuring markets have the strategic direction, insights, resources, and global guidance needed to develop locally relevant launch plans.
Capture and apply launch learnings across markets to continuously strengthen global strategy and execution.
Market, Customer, and Competitive Strategy
Maintain a strong understanding of evolving NSCLC and CRC treatment landscapes, customer behaviors, competitive developments, and market dynamics and assess their implications for LUMAKRAS strategy.
Partner with Competitive Intelligence, Commercial Data and Analytics, Medical, regional teams, and affiliates to identify emerging developments that could materially affect launch strategy, positioning, or execution.
Translate insights into strategic recommendations, scenarios, and potential responses that enable the organization to anticipate changes in the market.
Lead or support strategic workshops, market working sessions, and scenario planning designed to pressure test assumptions and strengthen brand and launch strategy.
Positioning and Messaging Evolution
Lead or support evolution of LUMAKRAS positioning strategy and messaging as clinical evidence, competitive profiles, customer insights, and market dynamics evolve.
Ensure messaging remains grounded in approved evidence and aligned with the broader brand strategy and intended customer behavior change.
Partner with Medical, Regulatory, Legal, and other appropriate stakeholders to develop and refine global communication frameworks and resources.
Ensure changes to positioning and messaging are informed by clear strategic rationale rather than developed as standalone communication exercises.
Global to Local Strategy and Affiliate Partnership

Let's get into the specifics. It’s impossible to capture every nuance of a role – especially at a rapidly growing company like Mews – but if we had to distil it into a job description (which we do because this is a job description), it would be this:

Product marketing at Mews is at a turning point. The function has been effective at launching products; what it has not yet built is the strategic layer that comes after launch – the continuous positioning, adoption strategy, and market intelligence that makes each product more valuable over time. This role owns that shift.
The Director of Product Marketing and Market Research is a combined senior leadership role responsible for two things that should never have been separated: how Mews brings products to market, and how Mews understands the market it operates in. You will lead the product marketing team, own the research and customer insights function, and serve as the go-to authority on both disciplines for senior leadership across the business.
Mews operates across property management, fintech and payments, guest experience, and marketplace. The right person for this role knows how to build a coherent positioning story across a complex multi-product portfolio – and how to ground that story in real market intelligence, customer insight, and competitive understanding rather than assumption.

Product marketing strategy
Define and own product marketing strategy across the Mews portfolio – covering positioning, messaging, and go-to-market execution from launch through adoption and ongoing engagement.
Build and govern the global product launch framework so that launches are scalable and repeatable, with clear handoffs between strategy and execution.
Own product adoption and post-launch engagement strategy – moving the function beyond launch execution to continuous market thinking that drives usage, retention, and revenue contribution.
Partner with Product, Sales, RevOps, and Customer Success to ensure product marketing strategy connects to commercial outcomes and is reflected in how the business goes to market.
Own NPS tracking programs and design the measurement framework for product marketing impact, including product attach rates, adoption metrics, and pipeline contribution.
Market research and customer insights
Own the end-to-end market research function: identifying research opportunities, designing methodology, running studies, synthesising findings, and activating insights across the business.
Lead primary and secondary research initiatives that inform strategic, commercial, and product decisions – including competitive analysis, customer behaviour, market sizing, and buyer intelligence.
Build competitive intelligence as a structured, ongoing discipline – not a one-off project. Translate competitive signals into positioning decisions, sales enablement, and product roadmap input.
Serve as the functional authority on what the market is telling Mews, and translate that into insight narratives that influence senior leadership decisions and business strategy.
Work closely with Strategy, Product, RevOps, and Marketing to ensure insights land where decisions get made, not just where they get read.
Team and function leadership
Lead and develop a team of product marketers, setting clear expectations, building capability, and creating a culture of commercial accountability.
Set the operating model for how the team works with AI – determining where AI handles execution tasks and where human judgment is irreplaceable, and building team-level standards accordingly.
Serve as the senior leadership go-to on product marketing and market intelligence – the person any executive can trust for a well-grounded, commercially-connected answer.
Represent product marketing and research in executive forums, contributing to annual planning and portfolio prioritisation decisions.

Professional knowledge and experience
10+ years in B2B SaaS marketing, with the majority of that time in product marketing – not demand generation, not agency, not brand-only roles.
Has held a Director, Senior Director, or Head of Product Marketing title, or a broader marketing leadership title that included ownership of the product marketing function.
Proven track record managing and developing a multi-person product marketing team, including hiring, coaching, and performance management.
Experience owning or significantly contributing to a market research or customer insights function – primary research methodology, competitive intelligence programs, or voice-of-customer work.
Deep understanding of B2B SaaS go-to-market strategy: positioning, messaging architecture, pricing and packaging alignment, sales enablement, and lifecycle marketing.
Experience building or significantly reshaping a product marketing function – not just managing an inherited one.
Has operated in a lean, fast-moving environment such as a scale-up, growth-stage, or pre-IPO company. Experience only in large enterprise environments with unlimited resources is unlikely to be a strong fit.
Skills and capabilities
Owns GTM strategy end-to-end – from initial positioning through post-launch adoption and continuous market engagement. Experience limited to launch execution is not sufficient.
Connects product marketing directly to revenue outcomes. Can articulate how their work has influenced pipeline, product attach rates, adoption, or retention – not just campaign outputs.
Translates research into business decisions – not just insight reports. Has a track record of research that changed a strategic or commercial direction.
Multi-functional marketing experience beyond product marketing, for example content, SEO, digital, demand generation, or go-to-market strategy.
Metrics-driven. Comfortable defining and owning the measurement framework for both product marketing impact and research quality.
Strong senior stakeholder communication. Able to influence executive decisions, present with authority, and earn trust through substance rather than seniority alone.
Publicly visible in the product marketing or insights community – speaker, writer, or recognised contributor to the discipline. Not a requirement, but a meaningful differentiator.
AI fluency
AI is changing the product marketing function in a way that is more structural than any other recent technology shift. A significant part of this role is deciding what that means for the team at Mews – what AI handles, what stays human, and how to build a team that operates at a higher strategic level as execution work is automated.

The Solutions Marketing Associate helps Sales create more quality client conversations while delivering fast, polished support for everyday opportunities. This role sits closest to the front end of the sales funnel: helping sellers identify the right accounts, do their homework, personalize outreach, and turn established marketing materials into relevant client-facing presentations.
For standard and smaller opportunities, typically $100K or less, the Associate uses existing positioning, narratives, templates, research, case studies, and proof points to efficiently build tailored sales materials without recreating strategy from scratch. At the prospecting stage, the Associate gives sellers the account intelligence and lead development support they need to earn more meetings.
This role builds the intelligence and inputs behind outreach but does not conduct cold calling, prospecting outreach, or appointment setting.
The north star is twofold: help Sales get into more of the right conversations, and help them show up to those conversations prepared.

Prospecting & Meeting Generation Support
Identify and research target accounts that fit priority audiences, verticals, solutions, or seller territories.
Build and maintain actionable lead and account lists with the context sellers need to prioritize outreach.
Research target companies, key contacts, recent business developments, marketing activity, competitive context, and relevant signals that can create a reason to engage.
Prepare concise account briefs and outreach inputs that help sellers personalize emails, calls, and meeting requests.
Connect prospect needs and business signals to relevant Digital Remedy capabilities, proof points, content, and conversation starters.
Partner with Sales on focused prospecting initiatives and campaigns designed to generate qualified meetings.
Track which research, prospecting themes, and materials are helping sellers open doors and use those learnings to improve future support.
Sales Presentations & Everyday Opportunity Support
Support standard and smaller opportunities, typically $100K or less, by tailoring existing presentations and materials to the customer and opportunity.
Build polished client-facing decks using established templates, positioning, solution narratives, case studies, research, and proof points.
Quickly identify the most relevant existing materials instead of rebuilding presentations from scratch.
Perform light account, category, audience, or competitive research when needed to make an established story more relevant.
Ensure materials are accurate, on-brand, easy for sellers to present, and aligned with established messaging.
Escalate opportunities that require original research, custom strategy, or a new problem-led narrative to the Solutions Marketing Analyst or Manager.
Sales Alignment & Enablement
Serve as a highly responsive day-to-day partner to Sales, understanding seller priorities, pipeline needs, and recurring friction points.
Help sellers navigate available materials, case studies, research, and solution stories so they can self-serve effectively when appropriate.
Capture recurring requests and content gaps and share them with the Solutions Marketing Manager and Product & Enablement team.
Support broader sales and marketing initiatives that create demand, improve seller preparedness, or accelerate opportunities.
What Success Looks Like
Sellers have a consistent pipeline of well-researched accounts and stronger reasons to reach out.
Prospecting support contributes to more qualified meetings and new sales conversations.
Smaller and standard opportunities receive fast, polished, relevant presentation support without unnecessary custom development.
Sales spends less time searching for materials and researching accounts and more time engaging customers.
The Associate knows when to activate existing materials and when an opportunity should be escalated for deeper strategic support.

1-3 years of experience in sales development, sales support, marketing, research, enablement, account planning, or a coordinator/associate role.
Strong research instincts and genuine curiosity about companies, industries, buyers, and business challenges.
Strong PowerPoint or Google Slides skills and good visual judgment.
Ability to turn research into concise, usable seller talking points and outreach inputs.
Excellent organization and ability to manage multiple fast-turn requests.
A proactive, service-oriented mindset paired with the confidence to ask questions and recommend a better path when needed.
Familiarity with CRM, prospecting, sales intelligence, and research tools is a plus.
Interest in developing toward solutions marketing, insights, strategy, or sales enablement.

We are seeking a versatile marketing leader to manage our marketing engagement across Southeast Asia.

As our first local marketing person in the region, you will design and execute a comprehensive GTM strategy that accounts for the diverse cultural, economic, and linguistic landscape of Southeast Asia, with a core focus on key markets like Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Thailand.

You will be responsible for identifying high-growth clusters, navigating complex regulatory environments, and building a unified brand voice that resonates across multiple markets. Your work will span social, influencers, partner, and event marketing. You will be at the center of the region's organic, outbound activity.
Location: Singapore (plus a few weeks at HQ for an extended orientation)
You Will
Holistic Regional Strategy: Design a scalable marketing framework that can be adapted for priority Southeast Asian markets and secondary markets across the broader region.
Localized Content Ecosystem: Oversee the "transcreation" and localization of all marketing assets. While English is our core working language, you will ensure our brand voice translates with native-level nuance across regions, leveraging your language skills where applicable.
Agile GTM Execution: Lead product launches across Southeast Asia, prioritizing markets based on data, barriers to entry, and localized product-market fit.
Cross-Border Community & Influencer Growth: Leverage regional social media and platform trends to build a loyal community through targeted influencer partnerships and localized channels (Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube, etc.).
Policy & Comms Collaboration: Work closely with legal and policy teams to navigate the varied regulatory landscapes, ensuring absolute compliance with local data privacy and advertising standards.
Event & Ecosystem Strategy: Develop locally relevant events and community initiatives across key priority markets, while also participating in existing industry events that support relationship building, market understanding and ecosystem growth.
Strategic Market Partnerships: Build and develop trusted partnerships with brands, NGOs, and platforms across markets to strengthen local credibility, relevance and long-term growth, while deepening engagement with creators, industry stakeholders and broader market ecosystems.
You'll Have
8+ years of marketing experience with a deep, pan-regional focus across Southeast Asia.
Independent Drive: Proven ability to operate autonomously within a strategic framework, driving clear outcomes with minimal day-to-day oversight.
Language Proficiency: Absolute professional fluency in English. The ability to understand, speak, or review content in Bahasa Indonesia, Filipino/Tagalog, Bahasa Malaysia, and/or Vietnamese is a plus.
Broad Market Knowledge: Experience managing marketing efforts in highly fragmented environments—from varying audience demographics and cultural perceptions to distinct economic climates across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, and Vietnam.
5+ years in Consumer Tech: Deep understanding of the Southeast Asian consumer journey, specifically mobile-first behaviors, privacy considerations, and local trust barriers.
Strategic Influence: Proven ability to advocate effectively for regional Southeast Asian needs (budget, product localized features, compliance requirements) to a global/US-based HQ.
Data-Driven test and learn mentality: Ability to drive growth and iterate quickly by being resourceful, analytical, and hands-on.

The Media Planner will be responsible for designing, planning, executing, and optimizing targeted media campaigns for suppliers under the client's Marketing project. In addition to campaign management, the role will act as a trusted commercial partner to suppliers, helping them maximize campaign performance, increase adoption of retail media solutions, and identify opportunities for continued investment and growth.
This role combines media planning, campaign execution, client relationship management, and commercial development , ensuring campaigns deliver measurable business outcomes while driving supplier engagement and revenue opportunities.

1. Campaign Planning & Setup
Collaborate with suppliers to understand campaign objectives, business priorities, target audiences, and growth opportunities.
Recommend media channels and targeting strategies using NIQ Segmentation Studio.
Develop campaign briefs, timelines, budgets, and cost estimates based on the retail client's rate card.
Advise suppliers on the most effective media mix to achieve campaign goals and maximize ROI.
Identify opportunities to expand campaign scope and increase supplier engagement.
2. Media Strategy & Optimization
Design and execute multi-channel media plans across: SMS
EDM
Push Notifications
Social Media
Other relevant retail media channels
Monitor campaign performance, analyze results, and recommend optimization actions.
Ensure all campaigns align with supplier business objectives and performance targets.
3. Client Management & Commercial Growth
Serve as a trusted advisor to suppliers and provide strategic media recommendations.
Build strong relationships with suppliers and key stakeholders.
Conduct campaign performance reviews and business discussions with clients.
Demonstrate clear business value and ROI to encourage repeat investment.
Identify cross-sell, upsell, and campaign expansion opportunities.
Prepare and present media proposals that support supplier business growth.
Support commercial discussions and campaign pitches when required.
Partner with internal sales and account teams to drive revenue growth and client retention.
4. Execution & Coordination
Liaise with the retail client's Marketing team for campaign setup, approvals, and execution.
Oversee creative assets and ensure compliance with retail client artwork guidelines.
Manage campaign go-live activities and troubleshoot operational issues.
5. Performance Reporting & Insights
Prepare pre-campaign opportunity assessments and recommendations.
Develop post-campaign performance reports and evaluation summaries.
Analyze campaign effectiveness and extract actionable insights.
Present campaign results and strategic recommendations to suppliers.
Use insights to identify future campaign opportunities and drive repeat business.
Maintain accurate campaign documentation, project records, and performance reports.
